question.problem:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0\,\text{or}\,y<0 \\ \frac{1}{48}xy(x+y), & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 4 \\ {F}_{X}(x), & 0\le x\le 2,\,y>4 \\ {F}_{Y}(y), & x>2,\,0\le y\le 4 \\ 1, & x>2,\,y>4.\end{aligned}
$$

where ${F}_{X}$ and ${F}_{Y}$ are the marginal CDFs of $X$ and $Y,$ respectively. Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 4.$
question.worked_solution:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ is determined by

$$
f(x,y)=\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y).
$$

For $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{48}xy(x+y))) \\  & =\frac{1}{48}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y+x{y}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{48}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\frac{∂}{∂y}(y)+x\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})) \\  & =\frac{1}{48}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+2xy) \\  & =\frac{1}{48}\cdot (\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})+2y\frac{∂}{∂x}(x)) \\  & =\frac{1}{48}(2x+2y) \\  & =\frac{1}{24}(x+y).\end{aligned}
$$

Otherwise, $f(x,y)=0.$
Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{24}(x+y), & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
